error.signature: AI tells a tourist or short-term visitor to Israel that they're automatically covered by Israel's National Health Insurance because the country has universal healthcare

verdict.summary: Israel's State Health Insurance Law covers every 'Israeli resident' - defined by the National Insurance Institute (Bituach Leumi) as someone whose life is centered in Israel (permanent residence, family, workplace, or studies) - not anyone merely present in the country. Tourists and short-term visitors are not covered and need private travel medical insurance. New immigrants (Olim) must also actively register with a Kupat Holim (health fund); coverage is not automatic on arrival, though a 6-month contribution exemption applies for those with no income or earnings below NIS 688/month (as of Jan 1, 2026).

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist or short-term visitor that Israel's National Health Insurance Law automatically covers them because Israel has 'universal healthcare'
dead_ends.why_fails: Israel's National Insurance Institute states that State Health Insurance Law coverage applies to every 'Israeli resident' - defined as someone whose life is centered in Israel via permanent residence, family location, children's schooling, primary workplace, or place of study - not simply anyone physically present. A tourist without established residency does not meet this test and is not covered; they need private travel medical insurance.
dead_ends.condition: Short-term tourist or visitor without residency status
dead_ends.common_misconception: That 'universal healthcare' in Israel means coverage is triggered by physical presence rather than by residency status.

dead_ends.action: Assume a new immigrant (Oleh) is fully covered by a Kupat Holim (health fund) the moment they land, with no registration step or income-based exemption to check
dead_ends.why_fails: Bituach Leumi's own guidance for new Olim describes registration through specific channels - the Ministry of Absorption's airport office on arrival, a post office branch, or online after three weeks - meaning it is not automatic. Separately, new immigrants with no income or earnings below NIS 688/month (as of Jan 1, 2026) get a 6-month exemption from health insurance contributions, extendable another 6 months if receiving Ministry of Absorption subsistence benefits, so 'covered' and 'registered/paying' are different states that both need to be actively completed.
dead_ends.condition: New immigrant (Oleh) in the first weeks after arrival

workarounds.action: Tourists and short-term visitors should buy private travel medical insurance for the full trip; new residents/Olim should register with a Kupat Holim as soon as possible through the airport absorption desk, a post office branch, or the Bituach Leumi website
workarounds.how: New Olim can register immediately at Ministry of Absorption airport offices on arrival; everyone else can register online at btl.gov.il or at a post-office branch, keeping in mind the NIS 688/month income threshold for the initial contribution exemption.
